open.description: C.SeekBar/default still FAILs (flat colour 1.15 %, region at x≈92–114 pt). The fixer did not address it. Evidence: Figma 1908:7387 draws the fill at x=2, w=98 and the head 'Rectangle 10' at x=92, so progress = (92−2)/(1238−4−8) = 0.0734. The Controls frame's own labels say 00:02:10 / 00:25:40 (130/1540 = 0.0844), which puts the head at 2 + 1226×0.0844 = 105.5 pt, exactly where our render draws it. Our geometry is right: seekHeadX is linear and the fill = travel×p + head.width reproduces Figma's 98 pt fill for Figma's own head. The fixture time also equals Figma's labels (videoApp loads 0:02:10 of 0:25:40, and C.CurrentTime/C.Duration PASS). The mismatch is internal to Figma. Honest fix: give the bar-only C.SeekBar/default entry its own fixture time at the position Figma draws (≈113 s of 1540, i.e. 00:01:53). Keep videoApp/product defaults and the time-label entries at 02:10, and keep the existing S01.ControlBar note explaining the label-vs-head inconsistency. Do not change the geometry and do not mask the region.

C-01: playNow now puts a one-shot ':start-paused' only on inputs[index]. I traced this against the engine:
- src/input/input.c:249 applies item options inside input_Create, and input.c:656 reads start-paused.
- src/player/player.c:85-94 has on_current_media_changed as the only sender, firing right after vlc_player_input_New, on both the synchronous path and the destructor-thread path.
- PlayerMedia strips the option under the player lock, which is the same lock the playlist uses.
- The real-engine bridge smoke (argv[3] audio branch, which runs in the fixture suite) proves four things: open paused while playing gives PAUSED, it stays paused for 1 s, the option has left the queue item, and replaying the item plays.

C-02: CanonicalMRL uses the engine's own vlc_path2uri, which matches how sidecar MRLs and their MD5 str-id prefixes are built (subtitles.c:346, input.c:2826). The case with ( ) or ' in the file name has no runtime test, so it is a live check.

C-10: the new two-baseline gate (snapshot and previous request) closes the revert-during-lag hole. I walked through these sequences and none of them drops a request:
- change then revert before the topic arrives;
- revert together with a resolution change;
- a stale intermediate topic;
- an outside hotkey change followed by a re-request.

The behaviour tests use a fake transport that publishes topics.

Hide UI OSD: app actions triggered by a key now go through canPerform, then perform, then osd.actionPerformed(keyFeedback). Menu triggers stay silent, and a blocked action shows only the key. The tests check the real OSD message and pressed-key text through AppModel.mock.

Other findings, all re-checked in code:
- C-03: the stream-only mode check is correct; the auxiliary-vout runtime part is a live check.
- C-06, C-07, C-08, C-11, C-12, C-14: fixed in code.

open.description: The entries of an extension's own menu come from the cached extensions catalog snapshot. The bridge fills that snapshot (extension_GetMenu) only when the catalog is rebuilt, and the menu bar rebuilds the submenu only when Observation marks it dirty. VLC's own UIs query extension_GetMenu each time the menu opens. If a Lua extension's menu() is not ready right after activation, or changes later, View ▸ Extensions can show a stale or missing submenu: the extension appears as a checked toggle row with no entries. This needs a live check with a real extension. It is not a blocker.

Accelerate is not listed in Makefile.am LDFLAGS. On Darwin, Swift autolinking (LC_LINKER_OPTION) should resolve it, as it already does for CryptoKit and ImageIO. The native plugin link was not run in this verification, so the integrator should confirm the libtool link at install time.

S68 is now REVIEW on all three engines (mean |Δ| 0.81). The remaining boxed regions are the D026 Mac shortcut glyphs. open.description: The guard decides whether a field is 'inside' the dialog by geometry: is the field's centre inside the dialog's rectangle? A text field behind the scrim that lies under the dialog's rectangle therefore counts as inside, so Tab can still move focus into it and the user can type there. The dialog is clamped to the window, so in a smaller window most of the content is under it. For example, Settings at 1048 pt wide in a 1280×800 window covers the library search field. I proved this in an isolated copy (scratch pkg, VerifyKeyLoopProbeTests.testTabFromDialogField and testGeometricHole). In New Playlist, Tab from the dialog's field reached a field behind the scrim 6 out of 6 times without the guard. With the guard it reached it 0 times when that field was at the top of the window, but still 6 out of 6 when the field was centred under the dialog. The same happens with Settings in a 1280×800 window: a centred field keeps focus after keepFocusInside. Fix: take the background text fields out of the key-view loop at the source instead of using geometry. MXRSearchField and the other TextFields would read mxrKeyboardFocusSuspended and become unfocusable or refuse first responder.

The Tab part of the test does not test the guard, so it would pass without it. It sends Tab with window.sendEvent, and that path never runs the guard's NSEvent local monitor; my probe counted 0 monitor calls. The fixer's report says NSApp.sendEvent, but the code uses window.sendEvent. The test also never puts focus in the dialog's own field first. From a nil first responder, Tab never reaches the field behind, even with no guard: the probe found it there 0 times. Only the part 'a focused field resigns when the dialog opens' is real. To make the test real, focus the dialog's field, send Tab, then make the guard's correction run, for example by calling keepFocusInside or by sending through NSApp on a key window. Then check that focus does not land on a field behind the dialog, including one placed under the dialog's rectangle.

open.description: After Stop, the player's on_stopping_current_media callback (reason USER) overwrites the bridge's `stopping` state with `finishing`. Until the player reaches STOPPED, the Convert hint changes from 'Stopping…' to 'Finishing “name”…', and the main button is enabled again as 'Stop', because it is disabled only for `.stopping`. The runtime test reads the state synchronously right after Stop, so it does not catch this. Fix: when `_activeJob.cancelRequested` is set, keep `stopping` in outputStopping.

The 'Audio — AAC (M4A)' output keeps the source's subtitle track. A headless conversion of Test Show S01E01.mp4 produced aac plus mov_text. This contradicts the hint 'Audio formats keep only the sound'. The runtime fixture has no subtitles, so the media suite cannot catch it. Fix: add scodec=none or no-sout-spu to the audio-only profiles.

J-10 UI part is still open: the two menus label renderer discovery differently ('Discovering…'/'Discover Renderers' vs 'Discovering Destinations…'/'Refresh Destinations'). Now that the bridge clears 'discovering' after 5 s, the disabled state is only brief. The files belong to other areas.

J-12: the pathFieldWidth token (buttonWidth × 1.5) is declared in the view file, not in MXRDesign as the fix asked. OutputProgressBar takes its height from Theme.Spacing.gap4, a spacing token used as a size.
The S37.Stream/running render is not deterministic. Its hint shows the build machine's own name (e.g. MacBook-Pro-2.local), because receivingURL reads SCDynamicStoreCopyLocalHostName.

The J-03 tests exercise only MockOutput's EEXIST behaviour. Nothing tests the view logic that decides overwrite (a format change renames the destination and loses confirmedDestination; confirmedDestination clears on completion); that logic exists only inside OutputMediaForm.
